question: Should OpenClaw standardize outbound installation/request attestation, and if so which trust authority, identity claim, and outbound request paths are in scope?
rationale: Source inspection establishes the missing capability, but code cannot determine whether OpenClaw should operate or integrate an identity authority, what a verifier may infer from a signature, or whether the permanent surface belongs in core configuration, the plugin SDK, or service-specific plugins.

options.title: Approve a narrow attestation RFC
options.body: Define an audience-bound proof of possession for a configured OpenClaw installation, reuse an established request-signing standard, and add only the generic plugin/request seam required by approved paths.

options.title: Keep attestation service-specific
options.body: Treat each external service as a plugin-owned authentication integration using its own API keys, OAuth, DPoP, or message-signature contract without a universal OpenClaw identity claim.

options.title: Decline agent-origin claims
options.body: Document that an open local client cannot reliably distinguish autonomous agent intent from a human controlling the same installation and do not add a general attestation surface.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow attestation RFC
recommendation.body: Define an audience-bound proof of possession for a configured OpenClaw installation, reuse an established request-signing standard, and add only the generic plugin/request seam required by approved paths.

likelyOwner.reason: They already own the active product/security review context and authored the closest current provider-attribution behavior.
